title: Floating-point equality through an EPSILON-tolerance is the actual contract
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE CONVERGED(NEW, OLD, OK)
C     Iterative-solver convergence test. The real contract is
C     |NEW - OLD| < 1.0E-6 * MAX(|NEW|, 1.0) -- a relative tolerance
C     with a 1.0 floor so the absolute tolerance kicks in near zero.
C     A naive port to (NEW == OLD) never converges; a naive port to
C     (abs(NEW - OLD) < 1e-6) is wrong for OLD = 1e9.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      REAL    NEW, OLD
      LOGICAL OK
      REAL    SCALE
      SCALE = MAX(ABS(NEW), 1.0)
      OK    = (ABS(NEW - OLD) .LT. 1.0E-6 * SCALE)
      RETURN
      END
notes: The 1.0E-6 literal is a magic number that deserves SME review (Phase 5 OPEN-QUESTION). The relative-with-floor pattern is critical to preserve — most reviewers see ABS-LT-tolerance and assume it's absolute. A correct port keeps both terms.
